rows.notes: The document is explicitly a review (journal section 'Review'; abstract: 'This paper reviews the most operational and explored methods based on optical remote sensing for the assessment of crop water requirements'). It reports no own data, experiment, survey or model runs on satellite-based irrigation advisory systems; the statements that satellite-based systems reflect actual canopy conditions, cover large areas and improve field-work efficiency (Section 3.3) and the IRRISAT water savings of ~18% and peak 25-30% (Section 3.2) are cited from other sources [58,144], not the authors' own results. Figure 2 (NDVI time series in Albacete) and Figure 4 (AEMET ETo forecast map) are illustrative displays, not an evaluation of the claimed water-conservation effect. Q1 is therefore 'no' and all subsequent questions are 'no'.

notes: Full text appears complete (pages 1-25 with references). Some pages contain duplicated/overlapping OCR text (pages 4-5, 14, 17) but content is readable. The study is a review article, so it cannot provide primary evidence for any claim.
